OBSERVATIONS.note: The frozen STATISTICAL_GATE is MU_SHARE_RULE > CONTROL_SHARE_P95. When the rule and control means are exactly tied, floating-point noise can decide the strict comparison. The frozen design is authoritative and is NOT changed here. Defense in depth is already frozen: PROMISING requires the practical (>= 0.05) and temporal (>= 3 of 5 years) gates too, so a lone float-noise statistical pass cannot change the classification. Covered by test_statistical_gate_alone_cannot_produce_promising.

year_side_matched_control_masks draws from every target-eligible row in the stratum, including the D2-abstained rows themselves. This is the frozen design function's own behaviour and matches the original D2 discovery comparator rate_matched_random_abstention. No new researcher convention was introduced.

Each replicate draws exactly K per stratum, so a year's replicate subset is empty only when that year has no candidate rows at all. Partial NaN across replicates is therefore impossible and is rejected explicitly rather than silently averaged.

F10_LONG_SHORT_COMPOSITION_MISMATCH.note: Per-stratum K equality is asserted for both sides in every replicate; K=0 strata draw zero rows.

F11_RNG_SEED_DRIFT.note: numpy.random.Generator(numpy.random.PCG64(20260922131)), N_RANDOM_CONTROLS=10000. Asserted distinct from the D2 discovery seed and the D2 BitMEX seed; same seed reproduces masks, different seed does not.

F12_REPLACEMENT_SAMPLING.note: rng.choice(..., replace=False) per stratum; tests assert each replicate sets exactly K distinct bits, which a with-replacement draw could not.

F13_DIFFERENT_MASKS_FOR_SHARE_AND_SCALE.note: AST tests assert exactly one year_side_matched_control_masks call and that both means_from_shared_masks calls consume the same masks object.

F14_SEPARATE_YEARLY_CONTROL_GENERATION.note: Yearly DELTA_SHARE uses year_means_from_shared_masks on the same masks object, subset by year; AST asserts exactly one such call and no second mask system.

F15_FUTURE_INFORMATION_MATCHING.note: The comparator receives only years, sides, target-eligibility and candidacy. No matching on PATH_SCALE, future volatility, future return, MAE, extrema or abs(BTC_RET_24H); an AST test asserts no share/scale array is passed.

F16_GATE_OR_CLASSIFICATION_RESCUE.note: classify_decomposition is the frozen ordered rule. PROMISING requires all three primary gates; PATH_SCALE elevation can only reach VOLATILITY_SCALE_COMPATIBLE and never rescues a failed ADVERSE_SHARE gate; the classifier never reads yearly or subgroup values.

F17_AUTHORITY_HASH_DRIFT.note: verify_design_authorities binds the D2 discovery RESULT, program decision, common.py, the D2 card and the arithmetic_mae module by SHA256 and currently returns no blockers; a mutated copy raises COMMON_SHA in test.

F18_ACCIDENTAL_REAL_OUTCOME_EXECUTION.note: execute_decomposition and load_canonical_core_btc_bars require an execution permit that does not exist; EXECUTION_AUTHORIZED is False and a forged permit still raises RealDecompositionForbidden.

F19_PROTECTED_2025_2026_ACCESS.note: construct_discovery_row refuses decisions from 2025 onward and the target re-walk refuses any bar at or after PROTECTED_START_MS. No protected partition is opened.

F1_LOOKAHEAD_FEATURE_OUTCOME_OVERLAP.note: Features (rv, ret, SIDE) come from frozen construct_discovery_row at cutoff E=T-5m. The target re-walk reads only bars opening at T..T+287*5m; a RecordingPerp test asserts min(read key) >= T.

F20_BITMEX_REUSE_FOR_NEW_TARGET.note: An AST test asserts the evaluator imports no BitMEX module. The surface is CORE_BTC_BINANCE_V0 2020-02-01 -> 2025-01-01 only.

F21_EXECUTION_READY_OVERSTATED_STUB_ROUT.note: The first review recorded EXECUTION_READY=true while execute_decomposition was a terminal stub that checked the permit and then unconditionally raised, so the canonical wiring would have been written AFTER the outcome-blind review. The complete dormant route is now implemented and reviewed: permit -> frozen snapshot identity -> frozen CORE BTC load -> C.build_rows(RULE1_INTERVAL_START, DISCOVERY_END) -> selector identity -> exact 288x5m re-walk -> frozen comparator at seed 20260922131 / 10000 replicates with identity enforcement and severity cross-check ON. An end-to-end test runs steps 3-8 over the real frozen interval against a synthetic surface. Frozen parameters are not caller-tunable: seed/N drift raises.

F22_PERMIT_AUTHORITY_UNDER_BOUND.note: The first gate let caller kwargs supply design/review/implementation/snapshot values and bound only run_identity to the permit file. The gate now takes only `repo`: every authority value is read from the tracked permit artifact and compared against tracked/current authorities (unit, design SHA, review SHA, evaluator SHA, CORE BTC snapshot, RUN_IDENTITY equal to the review's, seed, N, EXECUTION_AUTHORIZED, ONE_SHOT, RERUN_AUTHORIZED, plus the frozen selector digest and its version). A CONSUMED permit cannot authorize a rerun. Parameterized tests cover every wrong/missing field, tampered design or review bytes, unparseable permits, and forged caller kwargs.

F23_SELECTOR_IDENTITY_PROVED_COUNTS_NOT_.note: Counts are not identity. A canonical digest over the ordered (t_ms, selector_flag) sequence of the COMPLETE constructed-row population is now implemented and tested (equal counts with different firing positions produce different digests). ROW_COUNT_IDENTITY_VERIFIED and EXACT_SELECTOR_IDENTITY_VERIFIED are reported separately. No expected digest is invented here; the permit must carry one and the one-shot refuses metrics without a match.

F24_FROZEN_1791_MISREAD_AS_THE_ABSTAIN_C.note: Found while repairing F23. The frozen RULE_1_ROW_COUNT=1791 with 334/364/364/364/365 is the CONSTRUCTED decision-row population (RULE_ELIGIBLE_N), not the abstention count; the frozen RULE_1 abstention census in the same hash-bound discovery RESULT is 163 (10/48/32/23/50). The first implementation asserted mask.sum()==1791, which would have failed closed on correct canonical data and invited a post-hoc loosening. Both censuses are now checked against the frozen discovery result, which is outcome-blind for the new ADVERSE_SHARE target because it describes the selector only.

F25_CONTROL_PERCENTILE_CONVENTION_IMPLIC.note: P95 relied on NumPy's default interpolation. It is now explicit as np.percentile(values, 95.0, method='linear') behind control_percentile, recorded as CONTROL_P95_METHOD=NUMPY_LINEAR_INHERITED_FROM_D2, and tested to equal the historical np.percentile(x, 95) call form used by D2 discovery and D2 BitMEX.
